module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Primes congruent to $\{3, 5, 6\} \pmod 7$

Primes congruent to $3, 5, \text{ or } 6 \pmod 7$.

*References:*
- [A003625](https://oeis.org/A003625)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA3625

/-- A prime $p$ is in A003625 if $p \equiv 3, 5, \text{ or } 6 \pmod 7$. -/
def A (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  p.Prime ∧ (p % 7 = 3 ∨ p % 7 = 5 ∨ p % 7 = 6)

open Polynomial

/-- $3$ is in the sequence A003625. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : A 3 := by
  unfold A
  decide +native

/-- $5$ is in the sequence A003625. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : A 5 := by
  unfold A
  decide +native

/-- $13$ is in the sequence A003625. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_13 : A 13 := by
  unfold A
  decide +native

/-- $17$ is in the sequence A003625. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_17 : A 17 := by
  unfold A
  decide +native

/-- $19$ is in the sequence A003625. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_19 : A 19 := by
  unfold A
  decide +native

/--
Conjecture: Represents primes $p$ where the polynomial $x^2 + x + 2$ is irreducible over $\text{GF}(p)$.
- _Federico Provvedi_, Jul 21 2018

Answer: true, the equivalence is classical (complete the square: $4(x^2+x+2) = (2x+1)^2 + 7$,
then use quadratic reciprocity).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a003625-irreducibility/blob/d6c9f90827805142d81eee4e3d9099c8b48cbcc8/lean/OeisA3625FC.lean#L103-L104"]
theorem conjecture (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    A p ↔ Irreducible (X ^ 2 + X + 2 : (ZMod p)[X]) := by
  sorry

end OeisA3625

review.notes: Checked all seven declarations: OeisA3625.A, the five membership tests, and OeisA3625.conjecture. They faithfully state the OEIS definition and Provvedi's irreducibility conjecture. The prime hypothesis makes ZMod p the field with p elements and excludes the default cases p = 0 and p = 1. Independent Lean checks reproduced every displayed OEIS term, verified reducibility at p = 2 and p = 7, and found agreement with the no-root criterion for every prime below 1000. The exact cited external proof compiled successfully; its theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, supporting both the research solved tag and formal_proof record. OEIS web endpoints returned HTTP 403, so the full entry was read through OEIS's data mirror. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/OeisA3625FC.lean.
